Command replay (a class of call, not one reported incident)

Read the kubectl config with cluster credentials

What happens

Read the kubectl config with cluster credentials. The call below tries to read a credentials file. The agent sends it through its Bash tool, and it involves Kubernetes.

The call

cat ~/.kube/config

Tool: Bash. The replay uses placeholder tokens and hosts only.

Fix it without us

Give the agent its own kubeconfig with a short-lived credential and a Role limited to what it needs, and add a deny rule such as Read(~/.kube/**) for your admin kubeconfig. A Read rule also covers shell commands such as cat, but not a script that opens the file itself, so enable the Claude Code sandbox when the block must hold.

What KYA does

Replay result: Stopped. In the replay test, the local hook denies the call and names the rule.

Rule secret-read-kube, first stopped in version 0.33.0.

The hook is local and advisory. It fails open: if kya breaks or times out, the call goes ahead.

Install

For Claude Code, the host this replay ran on:

/plugin marketplace add The-Pixel-Boys/shield-kya
/plugin install kya@shield-kya

For any host:

npm i -g @shield-agent/kya@latest && kya start
